content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp historical spikes (e.g., 76+).
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to recognize that prices often revert to lower levels after peaks.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10 days; later days show more convergence with true values, suggesting a lag in adjusting to new data.
- Overshoots are more common in the middle of the forecast window (days 10–20), then gradually correct.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust downward quickly after a spike, even when true values show clear downward momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually align with reality — suggesting a need for early dampening of upward momentum.
